primary_source: Loewenstein 1994 Psychol Bull doi:10.1037/0033-2909.116.1.75; Kang et al. 2009 Psychol Sci (SSRN doi:10.2139/ssrn.1308286)
observable_feature: Hook text withholds the answer the body reveals AND a partial cue is visible (cut-off word 'doesn't exi-', 'The idea', 'Vs..', 'POV: you finally found…')
how_to_score: 1 if hook text matches a gap pattern (trailing '-' or '..'/'...' before the reveal; 'the idea/the problem/the concept'; numbered reveal) AND product/outcome partially visible by 1.5 s
our_evidence: curiosity_gap flag 6/10 hit vs 27/53 (FB); cut-off 'doesn't exi-' 91K

principle: Covered reveal works when the product cue shows (gap + stakes); a fully hidden product gives a gap with no motive
primary_source: Loewenstein 1994 (curiosity peaks at intermediate knowledge); Kang et al. 2009 (inverted-U)
observable_feature: At 0 s the product is under or as a cover (tray, muffin tin, cloth, drape) AND its own cue is visible (colour/texture/face around the cover, or a drape in the product's own fabric/colour); reveal by 3.0 s
how_to_score: 1 if hook shot motion = covered_reveal AND product cue visible at 0 s AND reveal_s <= 3.0; 0 if covered with the product fully hidden or a mismatched cue; NA if not covered
our_evidence: Covered (FB+IG) 5/16 ≥50K: 2.7M, 524K, 241K IG, 147K, 97K. Robe only 5/11 vs 21/48 other hooks (median 28.9K vs 15.7K). Cue visible 5/10 (median 63K) vs fully hidden/mismatch 0/6 (median 3.0K), Fisher p=0.09. Winners revealed at 1.2–3.0 s
external_evidence: UNVEIL staff-drape reels: IKEA X Christmas 17.4M and 755K (merryglow.official), COSTCO X Navidad 2.2M; tray reveal nocturne.robes 1.3M (corpus opening_archetype)
engine_use: allowed (D52); score the cue + reveal timing as an advisory, never block

primary_source: Sokolov 1963 orienting reflex (classic); Itti & Baldi 2009 Vision Res doi:10.1016/j.visres.2008.09.007
observable_feature: Unexpected event in first 1–2 s: fall, flare-up, chaos, absurd image, abrupt scene change on cut 1
how_to_score: 1 if hook shot motion in {chaos, fail, competitor_fail} or motion_0_1 in top quartile
our_evidence: F04 chaos 'then' openers 152.9K/70.4K/67.7K/40.3K(IG)/30.9K(IG); chaos/fail openers 3/6 ≥50K and 5/6 ≥30K (MGS-06 2.6K the exception)

principle: Open loop vs payoff (Zeigarnik; narrative transportation)
primary_source: Zeigarnik 1927 Psychologische Forschung 9:1–85; Green & Brock 2000 JPSP doi:10.1037/0022-3514.79.5.701
observable_feature: Multi-card arc where card 1 opens a question the last card closes ('Christmas 2024..' → 'Vs...' → 'Christmas 2026 🤩')
how_to_score: 1 if ≥3 text cards with a bridge token (Vs/VS/the result) and the payoff card in the last 40%
our_evidence: F04 multi-card 5/7 ≥50K incl 152.9K; winners 1.85 cards/reel vs flops 1.56

primary_source: Kahneman et al. 1993 Psychol Sci doi:10.1111/j.1467-9280.1993.tb00589.x
observable_feature: Last shot = most rewarding image (lit/burning/worn product, static hero, product share ≥0.6) + payoff emoji
how_to_score: 1 if last shot is a static hero with product_share ≥0.6
our_evidence: present on winners AND flops (table stakes, not discriminating)

primary_source: Cialdini, Influence (1984; rev. 2021); Goldstein, Cialdini & Griskevicius 2008 JCR doi:10.1086/586910
observable_feature: Others visibly wanting/using it: 'the whole street is JEALOUS', store crowd, neighbours reacting
how_to_score: 1 if hook text or a shot shows others desiring/using the product
our_evidence: social_proof flag 2/3; 'whole street is JEALOUS' 63.3K (n small)

primary_source: Worchel, Lee & Adewole 1975 JPSP doi:10.1037/0022-3514.32.5.906; Cialdini
how_to_score: 1 if hook text has RUN|sold out|limited|before Christmas|only
our_evidence: urgency 2/4; 'don't walk RUN to Walmart' 62.0K vs 'RUN to Target' 2.7K

primary_source: Regan 1971 JESP doi:10.1016/0022-1031(71)90025-4; Cialdini; Meta 'Fighting engagement bait on Facebook' (about.fb.com 2017-12-18)
observable_feature: Caption/end card offers something ('get yours', link) for a one-word reply; SAY not COMMENT
how_to_score: 1 if CTA with SAY keyword; flag COMMENT/TAG/VOTE as risk
our_evidence: end CTA card 'Say "MASK"' sits 60% from top; link captions are outcome-confounded (D6)

primary_source: Tajfel & Turner 1979 social identity theory; Berger & Heath 2007 JCR (identity signalling)
observable_feature: Hook names a group the viewer belongs to ('Christmas-aholics', 'cozy mom', 'ski dad')
how_to_score: 1 if hook text contains an audience noun phrase

principle: Gifting psychology (gift as relationship signal; giver–recipient gap)
primary_source: Sherry 1983 JCR doi:10.1086/208956; Flynn & Adams 2009 JESP doi:10.1016/j.jesp.2008.11.003
observable_feature: Recipient/gift framing ('the perfect gift doesn't exi-', 'women are hard to gift', 'send this to someone')
how_to_score: 1 if hook names a recipient or gift situation

primary_source: Brehm 1966 psychological reactance (book); Worchel 1992 BASP doi:10.1207/s15324834basp1301_7
Kahneman, Knetsch & Thaler 1990 JPE doi:10.1086/261737; Peck & Shu 2009 JCR doi:10.1086/598614
observable_feature: POV/OTS/high-angle hands holding, unboxing, using the product
how_to_score: share of shots with angle in {pov,ots,high} AND subject=product
our_evidence: fire-pit ≥30K: 14–43% high-angle hands vs ≤13% in flops; all reels pov 0.15 vs 0.14 (ns)

primary_source: Kahneman & Tversky 1979 Econometrica doi:10.2307/1914185; Cialdini contrast principle
observable_feature: Bad 'then' state → improved 'now' state with cringe→delight emoji arc
how_to_score: 1 if F04/F18/F19 with a cringe emoji on card 1 and a payoff emoji on the last card

observable_feature: Absurd-but-harmless image (ladder fall into tree, squad in identical goofy masks) + 😂/🤣
how_to_score: 1 if humor shot or laugh emoji AND no injury framing
our_evidence: humor flag 3/5 FB; BrickHood goofy squad 61K FB vs same video on IG 2.6K
engine_use: exploit in the BrickHood world only

primary_source: Sherman, Haidt & Coan 2009 Emotion doi:10.1037/a0014904; Nittono et al. 2012 PLoS ONE doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0046362
how_to_score: 1 if pet or child reaction shot present
our_evidence: golden retriever in all 60K+ MerryFire prompts; 🥹 POV 63K but 🥹 don't-show 0/2

principle: Sensory appeal / ASMR for calm content
observable_feature: CU tactile/sound beats: chocolate melt, flame whoosh, fabric texture, plug click; native ambient audio; calm song
how_to_score: 1 if CU sensory shot + named ambient SFX in prompt
our_evidence: named SFX boosted 1.3–3.4× on 8% of clips; calm songs on calm products (Omar rule)
external_evidence: robe texture POV CUs 26M; shelf liner 6.9M

observable_feature: Proven song at proven in-point; consistent house text style
how_to_score: 1 if song in the proven list at in-point ±2 s
our_evidence: Last Christmas 2:50, Bublé 0:32, Mariah 0:50 on winners
engine_use: exploit; fresh audio for variants (shadowban rule)

observable_feature: Awe/excitement/amusement payoff (lit house, roaring flame, squad hype)
how_to_score: 1 if the payoff shot is high-arousal (lit reveal, flame, action)
our_evidence: cozy_payoff 4/7 (FB); calm vs hype must match the product world (Omar)

principle: Self-referencing via first-person POV vs presenter
observable_feature: Face-forward presenter demo shots vs POV/OTS hands
